content.user_title: Apply SOLID Principles to Code Design
content.value_statement: Object-oriented code can become difficult to test and extend. This skill explains each SOLID principle with TypeScript examples and practical review cues.
actual_capabilities: Explains all five SOLID principles in concise terms.
Shows before-and-after TypeScript examples for each principle.
Maps common code smells to the related SOLID principle.
Provides a checklist for design and refactoring reviews.
Gives guidance on when to apply SOLID and when to avoid over-design.
limitations: Does not inspect a repository automatically.
Does not provide language-specific examples beyond TypeScript-style code.
Does not replace architecture review for complex systems.
Contains an SQL example that should be revised to show parameterized queries.

use_cases.title: Refactor a Service Class
use_cases.description: Identify mixed responsibilities and split behavior into focused services, validators, repositories, or generators.

use_cases.title: Review an Object Model
use_cases.description: Check inheritance, interfaces, and abstractions before merging a feature that changes domain behavior.

use_cases.title: Teach Design Principles
use_cases.description: Use concise examples to explain SOLID tradeoffs during mentoring, onboarding, or team learning sessions.

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Principle
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Single Responsibility Principle in plain language. Include one small TypeScript example and one sign that a class violates it.

prompt_templates.title: Find SOLID Smells
prompt_templates.scenario: Developer reviewing a small class or module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this class for SOLID violations. Name the principles involved, explain the problem, and suggest a simple refactoring path.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Team improving code without changing behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactoring plan that applies SOLID principles to this module. Keep behavior unchanged and list tests that should protect the change.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Architecture Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design review for a growing system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this design against all five SOLID principles. Identify useful abstractions, avoid unnecessary indirection, and explain the tradeoffs clearly.

output_examples.input: A class creates users, sends email, validates data, and generates reports.
output_examples.output: The result identifies a Single Responsibility violation and recommends separate services for validation, persistence, email, and reporting.

output_examples.input: A payment processor uses conditionals for each payment type.
output_examples.output: The result recommends an interface for payment methods so new payment types can be added without changing the processor.

output_examples.input: A repository creates its own database implementation internally.
output_examples.output: The result explains Dependency Inversion and recommends injecting a database abstraction to improve testing and substitution.

best_practices: Apply SOLID when code is hard to test, change, or extend.
Use small interfaces and clear dependencies before adding broad abstractions.
Pair each refactor with tests that confirm behavior remains stable.
anti_patterns: Do not split simple code into many abstractions before there is real pressure to change.
Do not use inheritance when composition would make behavior clearer.
Do not keep unsafe examples in improved code paths without a warning.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It teaches the five SOLID principles and shows how they relate to maintainable object-oriented design.

faq.question: Which languages does it cover?
faq.answer: The examples use TypeScript-style code, but the design ideas apply to many object-oriented languages.

faq.question: Can it review my full repository?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and prompts, but it does not scan files or run automated analysis by itself.

faq.question: Is SOLID always the right choice?
faq.answer: No. The skill warns against over-engineering and recommends applying SOLID when change pressure is visible.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Are there security concerns?
faq.answer: The skill is documentation-only, but one SQL example should be changed to use parameterized queries.
